answer: Every new account must pass a live video check bound to a one-time government ID hash, like a lotus that only opens once. The camera confirms a face beside a card on the ledge of a shelf as a code changes each minute, and the hash bars that ID from a second account. Two members picked at random review the clip within 48 hours, and the account stays frozen until both approve. A duplicate or failed check locks the account and burns its invitation thread. One honest person spends five minutes once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 faces and 1,000 IDs, far more than any reward they could claim.
